root.label: Industrial Revolution
root.gloss: How steam power, Hampshire wrought iron, textile mills, cholera slums, popular protest, and Chartism forged modern Britain.

children.label: Part 1: Steam, Iron & Mills
children.gloss: Watt’s rotary steam engine, Henry Cort’s Funtley puddling furnace and grooved rollers, factory child labour, and the 1833 Factory Act.

children.label: 1. Steam, Coal & Cort’s Iron
children.q2Chain: Charcoal Crisis & Watt’s Engine → Cort’s Puddling & Rollers → 1787 Portsmouth Naval Trials
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Charcoal Crisis & Watt’s Engine → Cort’s Puddling & Rollers → 1787 Portsmouth Naval Trials.

children.label: Charcoal Crisis & Watt’s Engine
children.gloss: Oak shortages and brittle coal pig iron held Britain back until James Watt’s condenser and rotary motion freed factories from rivers.

children.label: Oak Shortage & Brittle Pig Iron
children.gloss: Sulphur coal made brittle iron; Imported 50,000t Swedish iron.

children.label: 1769 Watt Condenser & Rotary
children.gloss: Partnered with Matthew Boulton; Slashed steam coal fuel waste.

children.label: → Freed Factories from Rivers
children.gloss: Ended winter frost stoppages; Powered urban coal boomtowns.

children.label: Cort’s Puddling & Rollers
children.gloss: At Funtley in Hampshire, Henry Cort separated coal from molten iron and used 1783 grooved rollers fifteen times faster than hammers.

children.label: Funtley Reverberatory Puddling
children.gloss: Separated coal smoke from iron; Stirring burned away sulphur.

children.label: 1783 Grooved Rollers (15x Speed)
children.gloss: Squeezed glassy slag from metal; Shaped uniform bars in seconds.

children.label: → Mass-Produced Wrought Iron
children.gloss: Supplied naval bolts and rails; Left River Meon slag remains.

children.label: 1787 Portsmouth Naval Trials
children.gloss: Admiralty stress tests at Portsmouth Dockyard in 1787 proved Cort’s iron beat Swedish imports, driving a 400% output surge.

children.label: 1787 Admiralty Forge Stress Tests
children.gloss: Twisted Funtley bars corkscrew-tight; Outperformed Swedish Orgrounds iron.

children.label: 400% Surge & Naval Independence
children.gloss: Forged Nelson’s Trafalgar anchors; Ended Baltic iron dependence.

children.label: → Built Steam Mills & Railways
children.gloss: Supplied tough machine frames; Underpinned industrial take-off.

children.label: 2. Factory Mills & 1833 Act
children.q2Chain: Factory Clock & Child Scavengers → 1832 Sadler Report & Crabtree → 1833 Factory Act & Inspectors
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Factory Clock & Child Scavengers → 1832 Sadler Report & Crabtree → 1833 Factory Act & Inspectors.

children.label: Factory Clock & Child Scavengers
children.gloss: Steam powerlooms crushed rural handlooms, locking workers and workhouse orphans into 14-hour shifts beneath lethal spinning mules.

children.label: Powerlooms Ended Cottage Weaving
children.gloss: Outpaced home family handlooms; Drove weavers into mill towns.

children.label: 14-Hour Clock Shifts & Fines
children.gloss: 80°F heat; locked dusty rooms; Docked wages for lateness.

children.label: Workhouse Apprentice Scavengers
children.gloss: Orphans crawled under active mules; Crushed fingers and scalpings.

children.label: 1832 Sadler Report & Crabtree
children.gloss: Former child worker Matthew Crabtree testified to Michael Sadler’s 1832 committee about 16-hour shifts, beatings, and deformity.

children.label: Crabtree’s 16-Hour Mill Testimony
children.gloss: Worked Yorkshire mills aged eight; Whipped with leather straps.

children.label: → Exposed Spinal Stunting Shock
children.gloss: Documented bowed legs in children; Shocked Victorian press readers.

children.label: → Backed Shaftesbury Reform Drive
children.gloss: Lord Shaftesbury led Commons push; Forced state factory bill.

children.label: 1833 Factory Act & Inspectors
children.gloss: The 1833 Factory Act banned under-nines in textile mills, capped child hours, and appointed four statutory inspectors.

children.label: Banned Textile Children Under 9
children.gloss: Capped ages 9–13 to eight hours; Mandated daily mill schooling.

children.label: Four Statutory Factory Inspectors
children.gloss: Enforced rules inside private mills; Checked age and school records.

children.label: Curbed Unbridled Mill Capitalism
children.gloss: Placed child welfare over profit; Pioneered workplace inspection.

children.label: Part 2: Urban Crisis & Protest
children.gloss: Back-to-back slums, cholera, Chadwick, and Bazalgette’s sewers alongside Luddites, Peterloo, Swing Riots, and Tolpuddle.

children.label: 3. Boomtowns, Cholera & Sewers
children.q2Chain: Back-to-Backs & 1831 Cholera → Chadwick’s 1842 Sanitary Report → 1858 Great Stink & Bazalgette
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Back-to-Backs & 1831 Cholera → Chadwick’s 1842 Sanitary Report → 1858 Great Stink & Bazalgette.

children.label: Back-to-Backs & 1831 Cholera
children.gloss: Unventilated back-to-backs and seeping cesspools spread lethal 1831 cholera through street pumps, shaking laissez-faire.

children.label: Back-to-Backs & Seeping Privies
children.gloss: Damp cellars; shared court privies; Sewage seeped into pump wells.

children.label: 1831 Asiatic Cholera Pandemic
children.gloss: Blue-skinned collapse in 12 hours; Spread via dirty pump water.

children.label: → Rattled Elite Laissez-Faire
children.gloss: Killed wealthy residents too; Prompted sanitary inquiries.

children.label: Chadwick’s 1842 Sanitary Report
children.gloss: Edwin Chadwick proved slum filth cut Manchester life expectancy to 19 years, leading to the 1848 Public Health Act.

children.label: 19-Year Manchester Life Span
children.gloss: Compared with 38 in Rutland; Mapped mortality across towns.

children.label: Economic Argument to Ratepayers
children.gloss: Drains cost less than Poor Law; Cut widow and orphan relief.

children.label: Drains cost less than Poor Law
children.gloss: Drains cost less than Poor Law

children.label: → Passed 1848 Public Health Act
children.gloss: Set up General Board of Health; Began municipal sanitary reform.

children.label: Set up General Board of Health
children.gloss: Set up General Board of Health

children.label: 1858 Great Stink & Bazalgette
children.gloss: When July 1858 heat fermented Thames sewage outside Parliament, MPs voted £3m for Bazalgette’s 82-mile brick interceptors.

children.label: July 1858 Fermenting Thames
children.gloss: Chloride curtains failed in Commons; Drove panicked MPs to act.

children.label: £3m & 82-Mile Brick Interceptors
children.gloss: Approved in eighteen days; Added 1,100 miles street sewers.

children.label: Eradicated Epidemic London Cholera
children.gloss: Carried sewage east past capital; Transformed urban civil health.

children.label: 4. Luddites, Peterloo & Unions
children.q2Chain: Luddites & 1819 Peterloo → 1830 Swing Riots & Winchester → 1834 Tolpuddle Martyrs
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Luddites & 1819 Peterloo → 1830 Swing Riots & Winchester → 1834 Tolpuddle Martyrs.

children.label: Luddites & 1819 Peterloo
children.gloss: Northern Luddite frame-breakers faced hanging laws before yeomanry cavalry sabred peaceful Manchester reformers at Peterloo.

children.label: 1811–16 Ned Ludd Loom Raids
children.gloss: Smashed wage-cutting steam looms; 1812 Act deployed 12,000 troops.

children.label: 16 Aug 1819 Peterloo Massacre
children.gloss: Yeomanry charged 60,000 crowd; Killed 18; injured over 600.

children.label: → Repressive Tory Six Acts
children.gloss: Banned mass political meetings; Deepened demand for voting reform.

children.label: 1830 Swing Riots & Winchester
children.gloss: Starving Hampshire farmworkers smashed threshing machines under Captain Swing, facing hanging and penal exile at Winchester.

children.label: Threshing Machines Cut Winter Pay
children.gloss: Burned hayricks across Hampshire; Demanded two shillings a day.

children.label: Dec 1830 Winchester Assize Trials
children.gloss: Tried 300 Hampshire farmhands; Hanged 19-year-old Henry Cook.

children.label: → Australian Penal Transportation
children.gloss: Exiled hundreds of rural men; Crushed open machine-breaking.

children.label: 1834 Tolpuddle Martyrs
children.gloss: Six Dorset farm unionists exiled under a secret-oaths law won full 1836 pardons after a 100,000-strong London march.

children.label: Friendly Society Wage-Cut Union
children.gloss: Six Dorset men under Loveless; Charged under secret oaths law.

children.label: Seven-Year Exile & 100k March
children.gloss: 100,000 unionists marched London; Delivered giant national petition.

children.label: 1836 Pardon & Union Rights
children.gloss: Crown granted full 1836 pardons; Anchored right to organise unions.

children.label: Part 3: Reform & Democracy
children.gloss: From rotten boroughs and the 1832 Great Reform Act to the Chartist Six Points and the 1872 Secret Ballot Act.

children.label: 5. Reform, Chartism & Ballot
children.q2Chain: Rotten Boroughs & Days of May → 1832 Betrayal & Chartism → 1872 Secret Ballot Act
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Rotten Boroughs & Days of May → 1832 Betrayal & Chartism → 1872 Secret Ballot Act.

children.label: Rotten Boroughs & Days of May
children.gloss: With under 5% voting and Old Sarum sending two MPs, Bristol riots and the 1832 gold run forced the Lords to pass reform.

children.label: Under 5% Vote & Rotten Boroughs
children.gloss: Old Sarum sent two MPs; Manchester and Leeds had none.

children.label: 1831 Bristol Riots & Gold Run
children.gloss: Burned Bristol Bishop’s Palace; £1.6m gold bank run in May.

children.label: → Forced Tory Lords to Surrender
children.gloss: William IV backed new peers; Enacted 1832 Great Reform Act.

children.label: 1832 Betrayal & Chartism
children.gloss: Shut out by the 1832 £10 householder rule, workers rallied behind the 1838 People’s Charter and three monster petitions.

children.label: 1832 £10 Property Vote Barrier
children.gloss: Scrapped 56 rotten boroughs; Excluded working-class labourers.

children.label: 1838 Six-Point People’s Charter
children.gloss: Universal male vote; paid MPs; Three petitions over 3m names.

children.label: Rejected Failure vs Long Victory
children.gloss: Commons rejected all 3 petitions; Five of six points later won.

children.label: Five of six points later won
children.gloss: Five of six points later won

children.label: 1872 Secret Ballot Act
children.gloss: Gladstone’s 1872 Ballot Act replaced open hustings with private booths and wax-sealed boxes, ending voter intimidation.

children.label: Open Hustings Bribery & Eviction
children.gloss: Public voting on wood platforms; Landlords punished defiant tenants.

children.label: 1872 Private Booths & Wax Seals
children.gloss: Passed under PM Gladstone; First sealed box at Pontefract.

children.label: Protected Independent Democracy
children.gloss: Ended employer and landlord fear; Fulfilled key Chartist demand.
